title: Energy-Structured Low-Rank Adaptation for Continual Learning
claim: Prior orthogonal-constraint methods leave knowledge energy dispersed across the basis; ours concentrates it into leading ranks, retaining far more energy at low rank.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid; three schematics plus a plot, with a shared legend
description: A 2x2 figure with a legend at the top left. Blue LoRA A/B trapezoids stand for past tasks and orange ones for the current task. Panel (a) shows parameter-to-parameter orthogonal regularization, with a double arrow between the blue and orange adapters, and is captioned 'Energy is highly dispersed (O-LoRA)'. Panel (b) shows input-feature SVD (U, Σ, Vᵀ) with orthogonalization against the adapters, and is captioned 'relatively dispersed (InfLoRA)'. Panel (c), ours, applies SVD to the ΔOutput feature, and a green-highlighted Σ shows the energy concentrated in its leading entries. Panel (d) is a line plot of energy retention against rank retention for O-LoRA (red), InfLoRA (teal) and E²-LoRA (gray). The E²-LoRA curve jumps to 100% almost immediately, and a zoomed inset with numeric labels shows the gap. Panels (a)–(c) have pastel backgrounds.
caption: Comparison of orthogonal constraints applied in: (a) parameter space; (b) input space; (c) energy-concentrated output drift space (ours). (d) E2-LoRA maintains high energy retention after rank truncation, enabling stable knowledge preservation (for past tasks) and efficient subspace reuse (for new tasks).
abstract: While orthogonal subspace methods try to mitigate task interference in Continual Learning (CL), they often suffer from energy diffusion across the basis, hindering knowledge compaction and exhausting capacity for future tasks. We observe that output feature drift induced by parameter updates is inherently low-rank, and theoretically prove that preserving parameters along the principal directions of this drift minimizes the output reconstruction error. Motivated by this, we propose \textbf{E}nergy-Concentrated and \textbf{E}nergy-Ordered \textbf{Lo}w-\textbf{R}ank \textbf{A}daptation (E$^2$-LoRA). By explicitly ordering and concentrating knowledge into leading ranks, E$^2$-LoRA frees capacity for subsequent tasks. Furthermore, we design a dynamic rank allocation strategy to balance stability and plasticity by jointly optimizing energy retention and model plasticity. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that E$^2$-LoRA achieves state-of-the-art performance. Code is available at https://github.com/kiddo127/E2-LoRA.
